findings.description: The new refusal always says "(pup land is finishing)". But a `pup land` that died after its `update-ref` (Ctrl-C or a throw during the audit, so `landed` was never written), or a fetch after the GitHub merge, leaves no land running. Every later `pup fix` then shows this message with no next step, when the right action is to re-run `pup land <id>`.

When `refs/remotes/origin/<target>` does not exist, `isAncestor` runs `git merge-base --is-ancestor` through `runGit` without piped stdio, so `pup fix` likely prints git's `fatal: Not a valid object name …` to the terminal even though the check correctly fails open.

In "undoes a round a pup kill took back to merged during the kickoff wait", the assertion that `killSession.mock.calls.at(-1)` is `[SESSION_ID, '%9']` is already met by the test's own `killPupSession` call inside the mocked `kickoff`. Deleting undoRound's new `killTmux(session.id, pane?.paneId)` branch would not fail it. Clear the mock after `killPupSession` and expect exactly `[[SESSION_ID, '%9']]`.

`takeFixRoundEdge` gets the id of the event it just appended by re-reading and scanning every event through `(currentFixRound(db, sessionId) as EventRow).id`, and the cast hides a possibly-undefined result. Returning `lastInsertRowid` from `appendEvent`, or using `INSERT … RETURNING id`, would drop both.

`relaunchWorker` checks `!isOwnRound()` at two exits, each with its own message, and the `catch` now has four ordered exits. `undoRound` also branches on the row's state to pick `killTmux` or `killSession`, and appends to the caught `error.message`. Folding the ownership guard into `undoRound`, and making the kill tolerate an already-merged row, would remove the extra branches.

`assertStillPinned` uses `merge.target as string` inside the `orNotStarted` closure. Binding `const target = merge.target` before the undefined check removes the cast. The function also now mixes the store re-check with the git landed-check, which a named helper would separate.
`startSession` keeps both `compile` and a destructured `const { compiled } = compile;`. Reading `compile.compiled.*` directly, as fix-round.service.ts does, would drop the extra binding.

The full `rm -r .worktrees/s1 … git worktree prune … (do not run git inside it)` wording is asserted in more than one test, so a change to `worktreeCleanup` breaks several tests. Pin the sentence once and use `toContain(worktreeCleanup(SESSION_ID))` elsewhere.
